name: LCI Industries
business: LCI (Lippert) makes engineered components such as chassis, windows, furniture and awnings for RV, marine and housing OEMs, plus aftermarket parts.

events.what: CEO Jason Lippert retired and left the board; director Tracy Graham resigned; Virginia Henkels named Board Chair; new Audit and Compensation chairs
events.from: LCI director; ex President and Chief Business Development Officer, Camping World and Good Sam

events.what: All-stock merger with Patrick Industries announced: 1.2440 PATK shares per LCII share, LCII holders own about 48%, about $150M run-rate cost synergies fully realized within three years of close, close targeted first half 2027; Patrick CEO Andy Nemeth to be combined CEO, Sirpilla Vice Chair
events.source: Baba document_id 50241 (M&A announcement call); merger 8-K not returned by sec-api Item 1.01 query (recall gap)

events.what: Board expanded to seven; new director
Director James Gero announced he will not stand for re-election at the 2026 annual meeting (date is the announcement)

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update found; the defining event is the Patrick merger close targeted first half 2027 (Andy Nemeth, M&A announcement, 2026-06-30, document_id 50241). Shareholder vote date not found.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Standalone frame is operating (EBIT) margin: 2026 guide 7.5% to 8% (70 to 120 bps of expansion) and a long-term 'double-digit' EBIT margin with no year, from the retired CEO and the CFO. The dated number is the merger's $150M run-rate cost synergy (within three years of a first-half 2027 close, so about 2030), stated by Patrick's CEO who will run the combined company; it applies to the combined entity, not to LCII standalone consensus. A 2022 Investor Briefing 13.5% EBITDA margin for 2027 predates the window and was not restated.

statements.quote: As a result, we continue to target 70 to 120 basis points of operating margin improvement in 2026 as we progress toward our long-term goal of achieving double-digit margins.
statements.speaker: Jason Lippert

statements.quote: These figures include the impact of approximately $150 million of annual run rate cost synergies with accretion realized in year one and all synergies fully realized within three years of closing.
statements.speaker: Andy Nemeth
statements.role: Chairman and CEO, Patrick Industries (CEO of combined company)

statements.quote: Given the success of our self-help initiatives, we still anticipate an adjusted operating profit margin in the range of 7.5%-8%. We are pleased that even in this challenging industry environment, we are able to maintain the original guided margin range.
statements.speaker: Lillian Etzkorn

street.gap_assumption: Double-digit (10%) EBIT goal has no year; compared with the furthest consensus year, VA FY2028 operating margin 9.88% (operating_income 424.8M / revenue 4,298.3M; calendar fiscal year so VA labels equal company years), gap +12 bps. VA FY2027 operating margin 8.17%. Standalone consensus does not include Patrick merger synergies.
street.source: Baba data_financials summary, fundamentals and consensus_history (pid 4250, FY-2027) cid 1003632; margins via data_compute

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin yoy: 4QFY-2025 +181.4 bps, 1QFY-2026 +85.6 bps (VA has not loaded Q2 2026). Reported Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin 9.3%, up 110 bps; adjusted EBITDA margin 12.2% vs 11.0%. But FY2027 EBITDA consensus fell 5.0% from 2026-06-30 to 2026-10-01 after the RV wholesale outlook was cut to 280k to 300k units from 315k to 330k; margin gains are self-help against falling volume.

verdict: Cheap and self-help is working, but the standalone setup is superseded: LCII is merging into Patrick (all stock, close first half 2027), its CEO left for an interim, estimates are still falling 5% in four months, and the street already models the double-digit EBIT goal; any GXO-style read belongs to the combined PATK entity and its $150M synergy target.
open_questions: Should the screen re-run on PATK as the combined entity, where the $150M synergy (about 2030) is the numeric frame and consensus may not yet include it?
Is RV wholesale (280k to 300k units in 2026) near trough, so the 5% four-month EBITDA cut stops, or are FY2027 estimates still falling?
Does the merger close on schedule (shareholder and antitrust approvals), given both are Elkhart RV component suppliers to the same OEMs?
